stem: How many T-states make up a basic 8086 bus cycle?
explanation: One clock period is a T-state; a bus cycle has four.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 2

stem: When is a wait state (Tw) inserted?

options.text: Between T2 and T3 when READY is 0

explanation: Wait states lengthen the cycle for slow memory and I/O.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 2

stem: In minimum mode (MN/MX = 1), the 8086 generates all its control signals itself.
explanation: Maximum mode uses the 8288 bus controller for some signals.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 2

stem: Which chip generates control signals externally in maximum mode?
explanation: In maximum mode the 8288 expands the status signals into control signals.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 2

stem: Which multiprocessor configurations does maximum mode support?
explanation: These are the three basic configurations.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 2

stem: What bits do 8087 coprocessor instructions start with?
explanation: 8087 instructions have 11011 as the MSB of their first code byte.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 2

stem: Two 8086 processors can be closely coupled.
explanation: The slides state that two 8086s cannot be closely coupled.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 2

stem: Which one is not an advantage of multiprocessor configurations?

options.text: Failure of one module need not stop the system

explanation: Multiprocessor systems avoid a single point of failure.
source: Case Studies Microprocessors and Microcontrollers.pptx, Unit 2
